description: The EPISODES platform of the EPOS Thematic Core Service Anthropogenic Hazards is a virtual laboratory for hazards caused by exploiting georesources. It holds episodes, which are time-correlated sets of seismic, technological and other geodata that link induced seismicity to its industrial cause across eight industrial activities, among them underground coal mining, geothermal stimulation and hydraulic fracturing, together with applications for seismic hazard forecasting, ground motion and source analysis, and a workspace with HPC resources. It is run by the TCS AH consortium within the European Plate Observing System to integrate research infrastructures on anthropogenic hazards. Coverage is mostly European sites, with some elsewhere such as the Cooper Basin in Australia, each episode with its own period; new geothermal episodes were added in November 2025. Access is through the web platform and an API; anonymous users can download open data and free registration unlocks the workspace. Licence: open data where marked, otherwise per-episode terms; free. Caveats: episodes are case collections, not a complete inventory. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of energy and mining infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the EGMS ground motion service for surface deformation around the same sites.
